clue.text: Get rid of beer a politician brought in

indicators.note: the politician and the article are taken into the beer, so they sit inside it

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get rid of a beer that a politician brought along.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out a practice or a disease is to eliminate it completely.

clue.text: Toy in Santa's fourth sack

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the named word is taken

parts.note: to rifle a place is to ransack or sack it

explanation.surface: A toy sits in the bag Father Christmas carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, treating it lightly.

clue.text: Nobleman's land, could be Roman

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's estate might date back to Roman times.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord's estate with its house and lands was his manorial holding.

clue.text: Pass beyond remaining launch

parts.note: something left over is remaining
to shoot is to launch or fire

explanation.surface: A rocket launch goes past its intended target.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot a mark is to go past or beyond it.

clue.text: A tower of strength at Southampton, say

definitions.text: A tower of strength at Southampton, say

parts.words: A tower of strength at Southampton, say
parts.note: a tower here is something that tows, a powerful one working in a port such as Southampton

explanation.surface: Praise for a dependable figure at a south-coast football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Southampton is an English port and football club; 'tower of strength' reads as a reliable person, but 'tower' means one that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful harbour vessel pulls large ships into and out of port.

clue.text: Winning hit makes one cheerful

parts.note: a side that is ahead or winning is said to be up
to beat is to strike or hit

explanation.surface: A winning shot leaves the player in a good mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An upbeat person is optimistic and in good spirits.

clue.text: American needing time for treatment

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A US patient needs time to be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is handled or treated, as in rough usage.

clue.text: Cheers short ball given treatment — from here?

indicators.note: given treatment suggests the letters are worked over into a new order
short means a letter is cut from the end of the word ball

explanation.surface: Spectators cheer a ball that falls short, wondering where the noise comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short ball' is a cricket delivery; trimmed it gives BAL, and with CHEERS it is rearranged. Bleachers are the cheap open seats at an American ballpark, where cheers come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators in the open stands are where shouts of support come from at a game.

clue.text: Family crest, inaccurately adopted by some

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any

indicators.note: inaccurately means wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms is taken up by people with no right to it.
explanation.definitionFit: One's family line, the forebears one descends from, is one's lineage.

clue.text: Intended one to replace king in European country

indicators.note: one letter is to be put in where the king's letter stood, swapping one for the other

parts.note: France is a country of Europe
R is short for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is meant to stand in for a monarch in a European state.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married is a woman's intended, the person she plans to wed.

clue.text: Grace is after good artist in a neighbourhood in Manhattan

indicators.note: the word for grace is placed after the first two pieces

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
grace in the sense of clemency or mercy

explanation.surface: A woman named Grace is chasing a fine painter around a New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: Gramercy, round its private park, is a district on the east side of New York's main island.

clue.text: A large painting outside

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a fresco is a painting done on wet plaster

explanation.surface: A big mural is displayed in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating al fresco means eating in the open air, out of doors.

clue.text: Grounds close to Marylebone ten clubs utilise

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to utilise is to use

explanation.surface: Ten golf clubs near the Marylebone area make use of some sports grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Marylebone is a district of central London, home of the MCC cricket club, which helps the sporting picture of 'grounds' and 'clubs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds as in reasons or justification for something, which an excuse offers.

clue.text: Deeply upset mother and father

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Both parents are deeply distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something sincerely, with deep feeling, is saying it with heartfelt emotion.

clue.text: Pet needs nap

definitions.meaning: a pet is a darling, someone specially favoured
a racing tipster's nap is the horse most strongly tipped to win

explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's pet is the preferred pupil, and in racing the nap is the selection backed above all others.

clue.text: Adam's mate's got to get hold of a sink and tap

indicators.note: to get hold of means to grasp, so the first piece wraps round the next

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner in Genesis
to drop is to sink

explanation.surface: Eve has to grab hold of the sink and the tap in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a phone line is to listen secretly to private talk.

clue.text: Declare in favour of state

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to state is to claim or assert

explanation.surface: A politician declares support for a nation state.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly and officially.

clue.text: 'Tommy' is a film based on a stage production

definitions.text: a film based on a stage production

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier
to be, to exist, is to live, so 'is' gives lives

explanation.surface: A claim that the rock opera Tommy is a movie adapted from a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' suggests The Who's rock opera, which was a stage-to-film work, but here it is a private soldier. Private Lives, a Noel Coward play, was filmed in 1931.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's comedy was adapted for the cinema, so the title names a film taken from a play.

clue.text: Loewe's partner playing host to a student

indicators.note: a host takes in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the lyrics to Frederick Loewe's music, as in My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: The composer's lyricist takes in a student lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject or skill.

clue.text: Immediately in agreement about opening of casino

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: at one means in agreement

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Two parties agree at once on opening a casino.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something straight away without any delay means doing it now.

clue.text: Clear area 100 ceased to occupy

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to quit a house is to cease to occupy it

explanation.surface: An area of a hundred units was cleared when its tenants left.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury that clears a defendant of a charge finds them not guilty.

clue.text: Lacking in self-confidence, gloomy Italian turned up

indicators.note: in a down light, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dim means dark or gloomy

explanation.surface: A gloomy Italian arrives, shy and unsure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DIMIT, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person is shy and nervous, without assurance.

clue.text: Sailor, very good on old instrument? Perfect

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
so as an intensifier means very, as in so good
the lute is an early stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A seaman proves a fine player of an antique instrument, simply flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good on' joins the pieces and completes the picture; 'very' alone gives SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and perfect both mean complete, utter, without flaw or qualification.

clue.text: Make merry around bar

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to revel is to make merry

explanation.surface: People make merry in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar used to prise something open is a lever.

clue.text: In conversation, agrees bloke shows charm

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: tallies means agrees and man is a bloke

explanation.surface: A man who agrees in a chat shows his charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky charm is an object thought to bring good fortune, like an amulet.

clue.text: Gorge at home during party

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone gorges on food at home while a party goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a deep narrow valley, the same landform as a steep-sided canyon.

clue.text: Threaten mischievous child on tip

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster is warned while standing on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the child's word before the tip's word, as in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends is about to happen and hangs menacingly over us.

clue.text: One may write a column about college caretaker

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a porter looks after the lodge and gates of a college

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a piece about a college doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist filing copy for a newspaper produces columns of print.
